Taught in the conservation section (claims c47, c48).

GK bank item (subtopic biodiversity): in situ conservation protects endangered species in their natural habitat; ex situ includes zoological parks and botanical gardens. Taught in the conservation section (claims c40, c41, c49), including NCERT's edition counts of biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries.

Real exam item: 'The word Biodiversity was coined by' — official answer W. G. Rosen (1985). The fetched NCERT text says only that Edward Wilson POPULARISED the term; the coinage fact is not in the source, so it is not taught as a claim. The section's exam_note discloses the distinction openly so the student can still choose Rosen when the question says 'coined' and Wilson when it says 'popularised'.

Real exam item: Rajaji (Raghati) Biosphere Reserve is in Uttarakhand. Specific reserve-by-reserve locations are not in NCERT Biology XII Ch. 13 and belong to ENV-06 (protected areas); not taught here. Source gap for this chapter.

Real exam item: IUCN headquarters at Gland, Switzerland. This chapter teaches IUCN's role (2004 species counts, Red List) from NCERT, but the headquarters location is not in the fetched source; it belongs to the Organisations book. Not taught here.

ENV-03.note: GK bank item (subtopic pollution): Stockholm Convention on POPs — adopted 2001, in force 17 May 2004, eliminate/reduce POPs release. Taught in s6 from the Government of India page (Dept. of Chemicals and Petrochemicals): in force 2004 (c53), India ratified 13.01.2006 (c54), POPs definition (c52). The adoption date 22 May 2001 itself is not in the fetched gov page and is not asserted in the chapter.

Acid rain is due to increased atmospheric concentration of SO2 and NO2 (official answer D). Taught in s3 with the full chain SO2/NO2 -> sulphuric/nitric acid -> acid rain -> marble cancer (hesc118, c09); also practice q12.

Layer that prevents UV rays from reaching the earth: Stratosphere (official answer A). Taught in s4: stratosphere contains the ozone layer which absorbs UV radiation (kegy207, c45); also practice q24.

Present in a refrigerator: Chlorofluorocarbon (official answer D). Taught in s4/s2: CFCs are used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays and damage the ozone layer (hesc118, c07); also practice q22.

Noise pollution threshold: official answer 80-99 dB. The chapter teaches the Noise Rules 2000 provisions that the fetched CPCB text carries (silence zone 100 m, night loudspeaker ban, complaint at +10 dB(A)), but no fetched source states the 80 dB threshold, and the CPCB page's Schedule with zone-wise dB limits was not in the fetched text. Source gap, disclosed in the s6 exam_note box; the number is not asserted.

International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer: 16 September (official answer C). The chapter teaches the 1987 UNEP CFC-freeze agreement (jesc115, c31) but neither NCERT source gives the 16 September observance date. Source gap, disclosed in the s4 exam_note box; students are advised to memorise the date separately.

Delhi's '15-point Winter Action Plan' for air pollution: a current-affairs item tied to a specific year's government programme. Not in any textbook/government source used for this chapter and out of the chapter's textbook scope; not taught.

WBCS Prelims 2016 Q62: 'Which is not a fact of Paris Agreement' — correct answer is the '200 countries' statement (195 countries adopted it, c28). Paris strands fully taught (COP21, below-2°C goal, c24/c28). Caveat: the option naming the '1997 Kyoto Protocol' is not separately taught — no fetched allowed-publisher quote for Kyoto was obtained (see REPORT.md gaps); the question is still answerable from the taught Paris facts.

Clerkship 2019 (Afternoon) Q31: 'Which does NOT cause global warming?' — answer: solar energy. Core contrast taught: burning of fossil fuels releases CO2 in large quantities (c05) and human activities drive warming (c04). Caveat: the deforestation option is not covered by this chapter's fetched sources.

WBP Constable 2021 Q64: with no atmosphere the Earth would be extremely cold. Concept taught: greenhouse gases absorb long-wave radiation and enhance the greenhouse effect (c07); the section deep text makes the 'necessary at natural levels' point explicitly. The exact -18°C figure sometimes quoted for this item is not in this chapter's sources and is not taught.

Clerkship 2019 (Forenoon) Q40: 'Greta Thunberg is an environmental activist' — a current-affairs/person item. Not taught: no fetched allowed-publisher source covers her, and a person-profile fact does not belong to this chapter's sourced scope.

ENV-05.note: Montreal Protocol signed 1987, Vienna Convention 1985 framework: taught from IGNOU Unit 1 (Vienna agreed 1985, in force 1988; Montreal agreed 16 September 1987, in force 1 January 1989) and PIB Kigali release (India a Party from 19 June 1992). GK bank item, subtopic conventions.
Basel Convention adopted 22 March 1989, in force 1992 (chapter gives 5 May 1992), hazardous wastes: taught from IGNOU Unit 1. GK bank item, subtopic conventions.

Convention on Biological Diversity at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit: taught from NCERT Biology XII Ch.13 and IGNOU Unit 1. The bank item's '150 government leaders signed' detail is not in the chapter's sources and is not asserted. GK bank item, subtopic conventions.

Convention on Migratory Species 'done at Bonn on 23 June 1979': the chapter teaches CMS (only global treaty for migratory species; COP13 Gandhinagar 2020, India presidency) from PIB, but no fetched allowed source (NCERT/IGNOU/PIB) states the Bonn 1979 signing, so that specific fact is not taught. Source gap.

Order Vienna (1985) -> Montreal (1987) -> Basel (1989) -> CBD (1992), with Stockholm Convention on POPs in 2001: all five dates taught in the chapter (ozone, chemicals_waste and biodiversity sections; chronology question q38). GK bank item, subtopic conventions.

Paris Agreement item (which statement is NOT a fact: 196 parties, COP21, below-2C goal, Kyoto parties' meeting): the chapter teaches only India's ratification date (2 October 2016, NCERT Contemporary World Politics XII Ch.6). The Paris temperature target, the 196-party figure and the COP21 adoption detail are not in any fetched allowed source, so the item's discriminating facts are not taught. Source gap.

International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer (16 September): the chapter teaches that the Montreal Protocol was agreed on 16 September 1987 (IGNOU Unit 1) with an exam_note box linking that date to the ozone-day question. The observance's formal name itself is not in the sources; the answer date is fully supported.

Layer of the atmosphere that prevents ultraviolet rays reaching the Earth's surface (ozone layer/stratosphere): taught — PIB Kigali release states the stratospheric ozone layer protects humans and the environment from harmful levels of ultraviolet radiation; NCERT describes the stratospheric ozone decline.
